To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IKKα is associated with Aurora A and regulates Aurora A phosphorylation.
IKKα is a regulator of the M-phase of the cell cycle and that this regulation occurs via modulation of Aurora A phosphorylation.
IKKα is associated with the mitotic regulator Aurora A, and regulates the M phase regulatory factors by modulating the phosphorylation of Aurora A at T288 residue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of IKK in regulating the cell cycle.
the role of the IKK complex in the regulation of the cell cycle and cell proliferation and the mechanisms by which this is regulated.
the role of IKKs in the regulation of cell cycle and proliferation of normal and tumor cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IKKα regulates M phase by modulating Aurora kinase phosphorylation.

IKKα is an essential regulator of the M phase regulatory factors, and its loss leads to the upregulation of the cell cycle regulatory proteins and increased histone phosphorylation, leading to the accumulation of cells in G2/M phase.

the IKKα/β heterodimer regulates the G2/M transition of the cell cycle and the IKKα homodimer regulates the M phase by regulating Aurora A phosphorylation, leading to regulation of Aurora A kinase activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IKKα is an Aurora A regulatory kinase and it regulates the M phase by modulating Aurora-A phosphorylation and activity.
the IKKα is involved in regulating the M Phase of the cell cycle via Aurora A.
IKKα is involved in the regulation of the cell cycle and this effect is mediated by the phosphorylation of Aurora A.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IKKα is a critical component of the mitotic machinery.
IKKα is an important regulator of cell cycle progression.
IKKα is an important regulator of the M phase and that IKKα may be a potential therapeutic target in the treatment of cancer.
